ai.purpose: Define the structural grammar of argumentation: argument tuples, node types, relation types, defeat types, failure modes, evaluation gates, operator roles, and phase sequences. SARG is the canonical engine for constructing, evaluating, and cataloguing structural arguments.
ai.summary: Book 7 formalizes structural argumentation through the SARG grammar. It defines argument tuples, node types, relation types, defeat types, failure modes, evaluation gates, operator roles, and the six-phase argument cycle. SARG integrates with TEL (Book 5) and NoS (Book 8) to form the reasoning core of the TriadicFrameworks canon.

references: INV-SARG-001: Argument Tuple Integrity — an argument tuple must contain all required components: N_A, R_A, C_A, and root(A).
INV-SARG-002: Defeat Validity — defeat types must be applied only when their structural preconditions are satisfied.
INV-SARG-003: Evaluation Gate Coherence — evaluation gates must produce coherent argument states under the SARG grammar.
INV-SARG-004: Phase Closure — all SARG phases must remain closed under the canonical argumentation cycle.
